title: Rav Shemaya II
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: He was a disciple of Rava. In [Eruvin 40a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.40a.7-8), Rava bar Tachlifa said to Ravina—Rav Shemaya challenged it—they went and asked Rava, who ruled in accordance with Rav Shemaya. In [Pesachim 25a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.25a.8-9) he raised a difficulty that Rava resolved, and in [Nazir 52a](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.52a.2-3) he addresses a query of Rava. In [Pesachim 49a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.49a.20) he is mentioned after Rav Pappa and says, “And they call him the son of one who folds his garment and lies down.”[^1] In [Pesachim 23a](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.23a.8) he says, “It is different there, for Scripture says ‘your harvest,’” etc.[^2]

notes.text: The phrase בר מך רבע is an insulting nickname, not a personal name. The William Davidson Hebrew text of Pesachim 49a:20 has Rav Pappa immediately before Rav Shemaya. Its English translation, and Rashi’s Vilna commentary on that passage, explain the last phrase as the son of someone who folds his garment and lies down to sleep drunk. Rashi explains קרו ליה as referring to the son. This source-supported interpretation replaces the earlier untranslated phrase; the English does not turn the nickname into an additional sage.

א״ק is the ordinary formula “Scripture says”; Pesachim 23a:8 supplies אמר קרא. The accepted transcription’s אולו שילו is rendered “they went and asked”: Eruvin 40a:8 has אזלו שיילוה לרבא. No different native spelling is established here. The terse dashes and unspecified pronouns do not add a new named chain of speakers. The heading’s ב) numbers this Rav Shemaya as II without identifying him with another record. All five cited passages were checked in the William Davidson Hebrew text; Hyman’s historical description “disciple of Rava” remains his own assertion, not an independently established biography.
